item.title: Shenzhen 'peace summit' underscores shared responsibilities of major countries
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
BEIJING, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- The first-ever face-to-face meeting between the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States in Shenzhen sent a clear message at a time of mounting geopolitical tensions: the world needs major countries to build bridges, not barriers, and safeguard peace, not fuel confrontation.
The historic meeting on Nov. 19, which Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi described as a "peace summit," saw the three leaders engage in candid, friendly and constructive exchanges on major issues concerning global peace, security and stability. It also produced a series of important consensuses and a declaration toward peace, demonstrating that even countries with differences can find common ground through dialogue.
Yet some have sought to frame the meeting as "Yalta 2.0," drawing a flawed parallel with the 1945 gathering of the leaders of the Soviet Union, the United States and Britain that helped shape the postwar order. Such readings are rooted in the old mindset of power politics and spheres of influence, and ignore profound shifts in the global landscape.
The circumstances and choices facing the world today are fundamentally different. The Shenzhen meeting was not about deciding the fate of other countries behind closed doors. Rather, it focused on how three major countries, despite their differences, could strengthen communication, manage disagreements and jointly safeguard peace and stability.
Chinese President Xi Jinping made four points on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace, calling for mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation. Together, they offer a constructive path for fostering sound major-country relations in a turbulent world.
Mutual respect and peaceful coexistence should be firmly upheld. Nations differ in their social systems, histories, cultures and development paths. Such differences are an objective reality of international relations, not a license for confrontation or interference. No country should seek to impose its will on others, still less treat another country's legitimate development as a threat simply because it is growing stronger.
Win-win cooperation is a practical necessity in a deeply interconnected world, rather than a mere diplomatic slogan. Global supply chains, trade and technological innovation link countries in ways that cannot be easily undone without imposing costs on all sides. Attempts to decouple economies, disrupt supply chains or erect barriers to technological cooperation may serve narrow geopolitical calculations, but they inevitably undermine shared development and weaken the foundations of global prosperity.
No country can secure its own long-term development by denying others' legitimate right to develop. The choice before major countries is not between one country's success and another's, but between pursuing shared progress and allowing zero-sum rivalry to hold everyone back.
Dialogue and consultation are equally indispensable. Major countries inevitably have differences, some of them deep and long-standing. The measure of responsible diplomacy is not whether these differences can be eliminated overnight, but whether they can be managed properly without escalating into confrontation. Maintaining regular high-level exchanges, keeping communication channels open and strengthening crisis-prevention mechanisms are therefore not optional gestures, but essential safeguards against miscalculation and conflict.
This is particularly important because major countries bear far-reaching responsibilities. When major countries live in harmony, the world is at peace; when they fight, the world is thrown into turmoil. Their interactions affect not only bilateral ties, but also regional security, the global economy and prospects for peace across the world.
China's vision of an equal and orderly multipolar world reflects this conviction. It's a world in which countries, regardless of size or strength, enjoy equal opportunities to participate in international affairs, differences are addressed through consultation rather than coercion, and international rules and institutions are upheld by all to serve the common interests of the international community.
Viewed from this broader perspective, the significance of the Shenzhen meeting becomes clear. It did not erase the differences among the three countries, nor could a single meeting resolve every international challenge. Instead, its value lies in reaffirming the importance of sustained communication, identifying areas of common ground and creating more room for managing differences. At a time when mistrust and confrontation threaten to narrow the space for diplomacy, that is no small achievement.
The world has already learned, at great cost, where division, confrontation and power politics can lead. What it needs now is not another attempt to carve up spheres of influence, but the political courage of major countries to respect one another, coexist peacefully and pursue the common interests of all humanity.
The consensus reached by the three leaders should be translated into concrete actions to build a future shaped by dialogue, mutual respect and shared responsibility.

item.title: Asia-Pacific Media Partnership officially launched
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
BEIJING, Nov. 21 (Xinhua) -- The Asia-Pacific Media Partnership (APMP), proposed by China's Xinhua News Agency, has been officially launched, with its first batch of members comprising 310 organizations from 41 countries and regions across the Asia-Pacific.
At the opening ceremony of the Asia-Pacific Media Forum held on Sept. 5, more than 400 representatives from over 40 countries and regions, as well as from UN agencies and international organizations, witnessed the establishment of the Organizing Committee of the Asia-Pacific Media Partnership Program.
The committee issued an initiative on strengthening collaborative communication between the media and think tanks, inviting media outlets and think tanks in the Asia-Pacific region to join the partnership.
Aiming to strengthen mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation among media organizations across the Asia-Pacific region, the APMP focuses on building four key platforms: high-end dialogue, collaborative communication, technological innovation and pragmatic cooperation.
It will regularly hold high-level media dialogues, promote joint interviews among Asia-Pacific media, jointly produce high-quality multimedia products, organize inbound reporting tours in China for Asia-Pacific media journalists, and host themed training programs for Asia-Pacific media professionals, among a series of practical cooperation projects.
Both the APMP and the Shenzhen Consensus of the Asia-Pacific Media Forum have been officially included in the deliverables list for China's hosting of the 2026 Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meetings. The Asia-Pacific Media Forum has also been included in the list of meetings and events hosted by China as the 2026 APEC host.

item.title: Trump calls trilateral summit with Xi, Putin one of most momentous in years
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
WASHINGTON, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- U.S. President Donald Trump on Friday hailed his "unprecedented" trilateral summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin as one of the most significant international meetings in years.
"We had one of the most momentous international summits in many years. That was the first ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China," Trump told a press conference at the White House. "And the relationship was fantastic between the three of us."
"The result of this historic summit was a first-of-its-kind trilateral peace declaration," Trump said. "The United States, Russia and China formally agreed that nuclear conflict must never be allowed to happen."
Trump also described the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, as "very successful."
At the trilateral summit in Shenzhen on Thursday, the three leaders had an in-depth exchange of views on maintaining world peace and promoting strategic stability in major country relations. Following the summit, the three countries released the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace.

item.title: Int'l Network for Silk launched in China to foster global cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
This photo taken on Nov. 20, 2026 shows the inaugural meeting of the International Network for Silk in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province. The International Network for Silk, the first global scientific organization in the textile sector to be headquartered in China, was launched on Friday to strengthen cooperation across the global silk industry, organizers said. It has more than 100 member entities from over 20 countries and regions, covering major silk-producing and consuming countries worldwide. (Xinhua/Han Chuanhao)
HANGZHOU, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- The International Network for Silk, the first global scientific organization in the textile sector to be headquartered in China, was launched on Friday to strengthen cooperation across the global silk industry, organizers said.
It has more than 100 member entities from over 20 countries and regions, covering major silk-producing and silk-consuming countries worldwide.
The body will operate as a global platform for dialogue, resource sharing and integrated development. It aims to deepen global cooperation in the silk industry, and support sericulture and silk sector development in developing and less-developed regions.
Silk production remains culturally and economically significant for China, which is among the world's largest producers and exporters of raw silk and finished silk goods.
The launch comes after China issued its first national guideline in September to boost the high-quality development of time-honored industries including silk, targeting stronger internationalization and higher positions in global value chains.
The country's first national exposition of time-honored industries kicked off in the east China city of Hangzhou on Friday, showcasing heritage sectors such as silk, tea, porcelain, brewing, traditional Chinese medicine, and arts and crafts.

item.title: China's high-tech FDI posts strong growth in first 10 months
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
A drone photo taken on Nov. 19, 2026 shows a ship arriving at Rizhao Port in east China's Shandong Province. (Xinhua/Guo Xulei)
BEIJING, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Foreign direct investment (FDI) in China's high-tech industries posted robust year-on-year growth in the first 10 months of 2026, official data showed on Friday.
FDI in high-tech industries reached 252.83 billion yuan (about 37.66 billion U.S. dollars) during the January-October period, up 31.3 percent year on year. It accounted for 41.7 percent of China's total FDI in actual use, increasing by 10.7 percentage points from the same period last year, according to the Ministry of Commerce.
Specifically, FDI in aerospace and equipment manufacturing, services for the commercialization of sci-tech achievements, and electronic and telecommunications equipment manufacturing surged 128.8 percent, 73.3 percent and 35.7 percent, respectively.
A total of 52,853 new foreign-invested enterprises were established nationwide during this period, down 1.7 percent year on year, while FDI in actual use stood at 606.93 billion yuan, declining 2.4 percent from a year earlier.
China's manufacturing industry attracted 143.04 billion yuan in FDI in this period, while the service sector drew 450.38 billion yuan.
During the same period, FDI from Canada, France, Switzerland and the United States grew by 105.7 percent, 35.1 percent, 23.5 percent and 9.6 percent, respectively, with investment via free ports included in these calculations, the ministry revealed.
High-tech and high-value-added industries have increasingly become a key focus for foreign investors in China, a report released in September said.
Multinational corporations are accelerating the establishment of R&D centers in China, positioning the country as a vital node in their global innovation networks, the report noted.

item.title: Xi's APEC speech inspires optimism for new chapter in Asia-Pacific prosperity
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-21
This photo taken on Nov. 19, 2026 shows the International Communication Center of Shenzhen, the venue of the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting, in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Xing Guangli)
* "If the Asia-Pacific miracle of the past more than three decades was a story of economic growth achieved through openness and cooperation, the next 30 years should be a story of shared prosperity achieved through inclusiveness and win-win cooperation," said South Korean lawmaker Kim Tae-nyeon.
* China's proposal to set up cooperation institutions focusing on the digital economy, clean energy and SME cooperation carries great significance and represents a key step in fostering new growth drivers for the Asia-Pacific, said Vitaly Mankevich, president of the Russian-Asian Union of Industrialists and Entrepreneurs.
* Georgie Too Hann Huei, COO of the Malaysia-China Business Council in Kuala Lumpur, said China is not only an active practitioner in the digital economy, clean energy and the development of SMEs, but has also accumulated rich experience in these fields, noting that China is now translating its development experience into concrete actions to promote common regional development.
SHENZHEN, Nov. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping chaired the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen on Thursday, calling for further efforts to build an Asia-Pacific community and write a new chapter of the Asia-Pacific miracle.
Experts said Xi's speech at the gathering outlined China's vision for a stronger, more integrated Asia-Pacific community, offering a roadmap for the region to build on the achievements of the past three decades.
They also said it could help deepen regional cooperation, create new opportunities for shared development and contribute to peace, stability and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific and beyond.
A SHARED VISION
In his Thursday speech, Xi stressed that building an Asia-Pacific community requires solidarity and mutual assistance, openness and integration, enterprise and innovation, as well as inclusive development.
These requirements are interconnected and mutually reinforcing, said Herbert Sima, director of the China Studies Center at the University of Auckland, noting they not only provide guidance for economic cooperation in the Asia-Pacific, but also offer valuable insights into addressing global uncertainties.
Solidarity and mutual assistance form the foundation of cooperation, openness and connectivity provide a pathway for development, innovation and progress serve as the driving force for growth, while inclusive development is key to ensuring that cooperation is sustainable and benefits all parties, the expert explained.
This photo taken on Nov. 3, 2026 shows a view of Shennan Avenue in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. (Xinhua/Liang Xu)
In his speech, Xi reviewed the achievements of the Asia-Pacific miracle over the past thirty-plus years, stressing the need to adapt to the new realities, take new strides and open up new prospects for Asia-Pacific cooperation in the face of new opportunities and challenges.
Xi's remarks have prompted experts to again reflect on the factors behind the region's remarkable economic growth and the prospects for its future development.
Virdika Rizky Utama, executive director of the Jakarta-based think tank PARA Syndicate, said the Asia-Pacific miracle had been driven by open cooperation, trade and investment, and the integration of regional industrial and supply chains.
What Xi stressed about building the Asia-Pacific community offered a response to the challenges facing the region and a vision for future cooperation, he said.
The expert particularly noted Xi's mention of "open regionalism" in his speech, saying that for developing economies such as Indonesia, the concept means access to broader markets and more convenient connectivity.
Tran Thi Hai Yen, a researcher at the Institute for European and Americas Studies at Vietnam Academy of Social Sciences, said Xi's vision comes at a timely moment, which addresses the four practical needs currently facing the Asia-Pacific region.
As the rotating chair of APEC this year, she added, China has further clarified the direction of cooperation and underscored the urgency of accelerating joint efforts, helping translate long-term vision into concrete cooperation agendas.
History proves that economies can prosper through trade with one another, and Xi reaffirmed the value of trade cooperation and open regionalism, said Craig Emerson, director of the Australia APEC Study Center.
A drone photo taken on Nov. 19, 2026 shows a ship arriving at Rizhao Port in east China's Shandong Province. (Xinhua/Guo Xulei)
Such remarks are highly encouraging at a time when trade liberalization has faced growing skepticism in recent years, noted Emerson, a former Australian trade minister.
"Economies in the Asia-Pacific region differ in terms of economic size, stages of development, history and culture, making the region highly diverse," he said. "This diversity should be regarded as a valuable resource. We should leverage our respective strengths, complement one another's weaknesses and turn these differences into new opportunities for cooperation."
BUILDING PILLARS TOGETHER
China is an advocate, promoter and forerunner in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation, and it is ready to work with all parties to pool wisdom and synergy in building the four key pillars of an Asia-Pacific community, Xi said in his speech. He also called for strengthening the pillar of economy and trade, upgrading the pillar of connectivity, fostering the pillar of innovation and enhancing the pillar of development.
On the importance of connectivity, Alvaro Echeverria, director of the Asia Pacific Chamber of Commerce in Chile, said the call to upgrade the pillar of connectivity was particularly relevant in the current international environment.
Greater proximity helps create mutual understanding, Echeverria told Xinhua, saying he welcomes China's call to strengthen connectivity not only through physical infrastructure, but also through continued efforts to promote human development and closer people-to-people exchanges.
These efforts could help rebuild trust at a time when the world faces considerable uncertainty and a lack of predictability, while the need for international coordination continues to grow, he added.
Xi pointed out that China is rooted in the Asia-Pacific and will continue to support Asia-Pacific cooperation, and announced that China will provide 20 million U.S. dollars to support APEC's practical cooperation, and to establish a Center for Asia-Pacific Community Studies in Shenzhen to conduct policy research and exchanges and provide intellectual support.
In addition, Xi said that in line with the needs of Asia-Pacific cooperation, China will set up cooperation institutions in such areas as digital technology, cross-border data flow, clean energy, and the development of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) to contribute to innovation-driven and green growth in the Asia-Pacific.
A foreign journalist takes a cup of coffee made by a humanoid robot at the media center of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Nov. 16, 2026. (Xinhua/Ren Pengfei)
"As a recognized technology leader in the digital economy, clean energy and related sectors, China can use these cooperation bodies to advance pragmatic cooperation among Asia-Pacific economies and build science and technology innovation partnerships," Mankevich said.
"This approach of 'getting its own house in order first and then bringing partners along' demonstrates China's leading role and exemplary influence in regional cooperation," he said.

item.title: Why Global Visitors Are Flocking to Chinese EVs in Shenzhen?
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-19
From automated parking and tank turns to ultra-fast charging in extreme cold, each technological breakthrough is redefining what's possible in the automotive industry. But beyond the technology itself lies something even more significant: China's innovation speed, R&D capabilities, and industrial strength.
From leading global EV sales to attracting attention from international industry players, China's new energy vehicle sector is making a major leap—from exporting products to expanding its technological influence worldwide.
One car reflects the rise of an entire industry. And what's driving onto the global stage is the strength of Chinese manufacturing and innovation.
